sections.title: Listening. Listen to a conversation in a shop. Choose the correct answers.
sections.script:
Assistant: Good afternoon. Can I help you?
Customer: Yes, please. I bought this jacket here last week, but there's a problem with it. The zip is broken.
Assistant: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Have you got the receipt?
Customer: Yes, here it is. I paid by card.
Assistant: Thank you. Would you like us to repair it, or would you prefer to exchange it?
Customer: Hmm. If you had the same jacket in black, I'd exchange it. But I'd rather have my money back, to be honest.
Assistant: That's fine. We can give you a full refund. It'll go back onto your card in about three days.
Customer: Great. And are those trainers in the sale?
Assistant: Yes, they're half price — only twenty-five dollars.
Customer: In that case, I'll try them on!

items.q: What is wrong with the jacket?
How did the customer pay?
What does the customer finally decide?
When will the money go back onto his card?
How much are the trainers now?

sections.title: G. Read the text. Choose the sentence (A–G) that fits each gap. There are two extra sentences.
sections.passage:
Dilshod opened his first shop when he was nineteen. (1) ___ He sold phone cases and chargers from a small table at the Chorsu market.

At first, business was slow. (2) ___ So he started making short videos about his products and posting them online. Within three months, people were coming from other cities to buy from him.

(3) ___ He used the money to rent a real shop and hired two friends. But he made a big mistake: he bought too many cheap headphones, and most of them broke after a week. (4) ___

Today Dilshod has four shops. (5) ___ ‘Don’t worry about failing,’ he says. ‘Worry about not trying.’
